title: Twists are well-defined on the common-finite-stage coefficient category
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], fix $m\in\mathbf Z$, and let $\mathcal C_S=D^b_c(S,\Qlb)$ be the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For each finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ contained in $\Qlb$, let $T_{E,m}$ be the rational twist functor induced on integral representatives by tensoring with $\mathcal O_E(m)$ [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Assume the finite-stage inverse identities $T_{E,-m}T_{E,m}\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $T_{E,m}T_{E,-m}\cong\mathrm{id}$ given by line evaluation. Write $B_{F/E}$ for scalar extension from $E$ to $F$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and use the natural comparisons $\beta_{F/E,C}:B_{F/E}(T_{E,m}C)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{F,m}(B_{F/E}C)$ of [lem-weil-integral-twist-derived-scalar] after rationalization. Assume their identity and tower compatibility of [lem-weil-integral-twist-scalar-coherence] and their compatibility with line evaluation of [lem-weil-integral-twist-base-change], for $m$ and $-m$. Then the assignment $(E,C)\mapsto(E,T_{E,m}C)$ defines a functor on $\mathcal C_S$: for a representative $[F,f]:(E,C)\to(E',C')$, where $f:B_{F/E}C\to B_{F/E'}C'$, its image is represented by
$$
 [F,\,\beta_{F/E',C'}^{-1}\circ T_{F,m}(f)\circ\beta_{F/E,C}].
$$
Equivalently it is $[F,T_{F,m}(f)]$ after identifying the endpoints by $\beta$. This class is independent of enlarging $F$, and composition is preserved. The line-evaluation inverse identities descend through these same comparisons. The resulting functor $T_m:\mathcal C_S\to\mathcal C_S$ has inverse $T_{-m}$, so $\Qlb(m)$ is invertible in the common-stage category.
